claim.quote: We present the first continuous operation in a surface lab of BULLKID, a detector for searches of light Dark Matter and precision measurements of the coherent and elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering.

key_value.note: Energy threshold of the surface run.

name: Low-energy spectrum of the BULLKID detector array operated on surface
notes: Surface run at Sapienza University (no shields); a detector characterisation, not a dark matter search.

summary.plain: A BULLKID array of 60 silicon blocks was run continuously for the first time in a surface laboratory. It reached a threshold of 160 electronvolts and could reject background events that hit more than one block.
summary.technical: 60 cubic silicon absorbers of 0.34 g each sensed by cryogenic KIDs, 39 hours of ambient background without shields: flat spectrum at (2.0 +- 0.1 stat +- 0.2 syst) x 10^6 counts/keV/kg/day down to a threshold of 160 +- 13 eV; the segmented monolithic structure rejects backgrounds from interactions in other array sites.

title: Low-energy spectrum of the BULLKID detector array operated on surface
why_it_matters: The abstract states the analysis demonstrates the unique capability of rejecting backgrounds generated from interactions in other sites of the array.
